note: Gathered and written by a machine from public sources and checked against them. Not reviewed by a person, not rights-cleared, not tested on learners. The rules are in manifest.json.

card.name: Bulgarian folk dance
card.era: Pre-Christian/Thracian roots; systematically collected from the 19th century
card.tagline: The umbrella tradition of Bulgarian chain/line dancing.
card.profile: The broad category of Bulgarian folk dance, overwhelmingly built on the horo (хоро) chain/line dance plus the solo/couple rachenitsa. Defined by asymmetrical 'Bulgarian rhythms' (short=2, long=3 units) producing 5/8, 7/8, 9/8, 11/16, 13/16 and 15/16 meters across seven ethnographic regions. Handholds include the V (down), W (shoulder height), shoulder hold and belt-hold (na lesa). Instruments: gaida, gadulka, kaval, tambura and tapan. Danced at weddings, holidays and village gatherings (English Wikipedia; Britannica).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologist Timothy Rice's fieldwork found each generic dance name is tied to a unique repeating pattern of unequal short and long beats; the national repertoire is commonly cited at ~300 chain dances (Radio Bulgaria/BNR, quoting the Taratanci Foundation).

observation.formation_and_space: initially scattered, then a line, then a circle
observation.posture: upright torso, knees slightly bent, weight shifts between feet
observation.footwork: rhythmic stepping, including hops, kicks, and stamps, synchronized with the music
observation.arms_and_hands: arms held high, hands joined in a line or circle, some dancers hold drums
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal movement, focus on leg and foot coordination
observation.partnering: dancers hold hands in a line or circle
observation.levels_jumps_turns: jumps, hops, and some dancers perform on top of drums
observation.costume_and_props: traditional Bulgarian folk costumes, including white shirts, vests, and trousers, some dancers carry drums
observation.cannot_infer: low resolution makes it difficult to see exact foot placement and weight transfer

signature_moments.what: dancers move in a line, stepping in unison with drums
dancers stand on top of their drums, holding hands in a circle, and perform a series of hops and kicks
